source.title: The Role of Early Bioelectric Signals in the Regeneration of Planarian Anterior/Posterior Polarity

stage: trunk fragment (post-pharyngeal to mid-tail, PT fragment)
injury: transverse cuts immediately posterior to the pharynx and halfway to the tail tip (PT fragment)

intervention.description: PT fragments placed in 0.24 uM nigericin + 15 mM potassium gluconate immediately after cutting for 3 h, washed three times, then regenerated in spring water.

readout.method: dissecting-microscope scoring of eyes at the anterior and posterior poles

notes: Text: 13% double-headed, 'the remaining 87%' normal single-headed. N=132 is from the Fisher-test parenthetical in the Fig 2B legend and may include controls (ambiguous), so n_total is low confidence. 13% of 132 = 17.2 -> 17. Pooled from at least three replicate experiments.
remainder_quote: The remaining 87% of animals regenerating in nigericin solution formed morphologically normal single-headed worms, indistinguishable from controls, with no intermediate phenotypes.

source.title: The Role of Early Bioelectric Signals in the Regeneration of Planarian Anterior/Posterior Polarity
source.location: Fig2B legend; main text Results section 2

stage: trunk fragment (cut immediately posterior to pharynx and midway to tail tip; PT fragment)
injury: transverse amputation immediately posterior to the pharynx and halfway between pharynx and tail tip

intervention.description: Fragments were soaked in 0.0024% ethanol in water for 3 h after cutting, then washed and kept in water.

readout.method: Scored by eye under dissecting microscope for eye placement at both poles

notes: Text: 0% double-headed in controls (Fig 2Bc); legend: controls 'in which this phenotype was not observed'. No n for controls. Normal set to 100% from the legend sentence describing the regenerative outcome of the control treatment as single-headed, and the text calling treated normals 'indistinguishable from controls'; percentage only, low confidence.
remainder_quote: Regenerative outcome of the control treatment, showing a single-headed worm, with a head at the anterior (b) and a tail at the posterior (c)

source.title: The Role of Early Bioelectric Signals in the Regeneration of Planarian Anterior/Posterior Polarity

stage: trunk fragment (post-pharyngeal to mid-tail, PT fragment)
injury: transverse cuts immediately posterior to the pharynx and halfway to the tail tip (PT fragment)

intervention.description: Whole worms presoaked in potassium gluconate (no nigericin) for one week, then cut into PT fragments and allowed to regenerate.

readout.method: dissecting-microscope scoring of eyes at the anterior and posterior poles

notes: 8% double-headed (N=60) 'of regenerated treated worms'. 8% of 60 = 4.8 -> 5. Potassium gluconate concentration and whether exposure continued after amputation are not stated. Other outcomes not described: partial. The matching control (0%, no n, solution not described) cannot be encoded and is not a row.
